name: maybe_Ui_PanelState_AwardPrize
summary: Casino prize panel step handler: plays SE 5 (or cue 0x39) while the panel sits in state 0x28, then once the cue finishes awards the pending prize. Prize id 0x2E is gold - it writes the new total through 0x0061251C into bag work +0x24A98 and animates the payout gauge from the old to the new amount; any other id is an item, granted by 0x0035EBB0(work, itemId, count) and announced by formatting the item name into state 2.
evidence: The panel is the casino poker/prize base class, not a party panel: its constructor Ui_PokerWindow_Ctor (0x001E3E78) installs g_uiPokerWindowBaseVtable, and the same 0x1E2xxx block already holds Ui_Panel_Reset / Ui_PanelState_Enter0B / Enter0EOr10 / Enter16. The two branches are a prize award: 0x0061251C is the gold setter (same call as the gold branch of 0x001E2A90/0x001E2B70) and 0x0035EBB0(work, f_240, f_244) is the item grant, followed by Item_LookupRecord + Text_FormatMessageArg for the item name. Nothing here highlights anything, so 'UpdateHighlight' was wrong.

name: Ui_MessagePanel_HandleConfirm
summary: Confirm handler of the message/talk panel: pops the pane stack, and when the prompt reports the first choice confirmed it emits the icon-select entry list, stores the selected scroll row in bag work and pushes the result pane; otherwise it emits the empty-message opcode with 0xFFFF ids. Both paths rebind the +0x1EE4 control slot.
evidence: Named callees pin the class: Ui_PaneStack_Pop and Ui_MessagePanel_PushPane with g_uiMessagePanelStateCallbacks, plus Ui_PromptRef_IsFirstChoiceConfirmed and Container_SmallVectorInitFrom over panel->iconSelect. Its exact counterpart 0x003B0D70 (same func_003B0F44 + Ui_Slot_BindControl + func_00123594 triple) is the empty path, so the pair is the confirm/empty pair of one panel handler.

name: maybe_Ui_PanelState_IncreaseBet
summary: Raises the casino bet by one step: while the bet counter at +0x22C is below 10 it compares current gold (0x0066B2CC on bag work +0x24A98) plus the stake from 0x0062F9B0 against the 9,999,999 cap and enters state 6 (accepted, stake*2, bet+1) or state 7 (not affordable); at 10 it enters state 0x0F and arms a 5-frame delay. The leading block is the inlined lazy init of the shared 0x1EB0 anim-sequence object plus BGM request 0x20, not the function's purpose.
evidence: Both callers are bet paths: Ui_PokerCards_ApplyBetMultiplier (0x00295280) -> 0x001E1BA4 -> here, and 0x001E1D98 which also calls Ui_PartyPanel_SelectSlot. The 0x0098967F gold cap and the 0x0066B2CC gold read are the FACTS.md bag-work gold accessors, and the two outcomes are the accept/reject pair of a bet. 'EnsureSlotObjects' described only the inlined allocator boilerplate.

name: maybe_Ui_PanelState_FinishPayout
summary: Completion half of one casino payout step: ticks the +0x19C cue, plays cue 0x3A (or 0x3B in mode 2) at state 0x37, then once the cue is done commits the new gold total at +0x23C into bag work, animates the payout gauge from the current gold to that total and restarts the step at state 1.
evidence: Same callee set as its sibling 0x001E2A90 (Ui_SlotWindow_SetupPayoutGauge, 0x0061251C gold write, Ui_Slot_BindControl, g_uiPartyPanelSlotObjectCallbacks step pair) but it runs after the cue instead of before, so it is the finish half of the payout count-up. The class is the casino panel (Ui_PokerWindow_Ctor installs g_uiPokerWindowBaseVtable), not a party panel.

name: Ui_PanelState_Enter11Or0E
summary: Panel-state transition: waits for the payout-gauge step and clears the list selection, then enters state 0x11 (selecting the row and rebinding the slot) when a row id is set, or state 0x0E with a -1 row id when none is.
evidence: The name already matches the cluster's established convention - the same 0x1E2xxx block holds Ui_PanelState_Enter0B, Ui_PanelState_Enter0EOr10, Ui_PanelState_Enter16 and Ui_PanelState_Enter09ForRow, all with the identical 'func_001E3BEC(panel, state) + Ui_Slot_BindControl + g_uiPartyPanelSlotObjectCallbacks step pair' shape. Its only caller 0x001E30B8 is the idle variant of the same transition.

name: maybe_Ui_PanelState_StartPayout
summary: Starts one casino payout step: after the +0x224 delay expires it commits the new gold total from 0x0062F89C into bag work, enters state 1 and animates the payout gauge from the current gold to that total, then rebinds the slot control and installs the next step-handler pair.
evidence: 0x0061251C is the gold setter (the gold branch of 0x001E338C uses it the same way) and Ui_SlotWindow_SetupPayoutGauge takes (oldGold, newGold, 0x1E, 10, 10), i.e. a count-up animation. Paired with 0x001E2B70 which does the same after the cue, so this is the start half. Class is the casino panel, not a party panel.

name: maybe_Ui_PanelState_SelectStepPair

evidence: The body only ever writes panel->f_30/f_34 (the step-handler pair) from g_uiPartyPanelSlotObjectCallbacks indices 0/1, 0x24/0x25 and 0x26/0x27, plus one func_001E3BEC(panel,0x13) state change - there is no page or text handling, so 'AdvancePage' was wrong. Class is the casino panel (Ui_PokerWindow_Ctor installs g_uiPokerWindowBaseVtable).

name: maybe_Item_AddRandomizedToInventory

The 0x1869F (99999) default and the per-item byte table at +0x49 are new; nothing here randomizes equipment *slots*, so the old name described the wrong object.

name: Ui_DataPanel_OpenWithFlags

It then stamps the time hash into work+0x2D418/+0x2FAF8, copies the 31 member snapshots into panel+0x1830, copies the save work, binds the label panes and enters state 5.

name: Ui_DiveForm_UpdateCommandList
summary: Dive-form handler-table slot 14 (table 0x0072C4C8, entry 0x0072C538), run once per frame while the dive form is up: honours the 'closing' bit of the form state u16, then either forwards the three signed stick bytes to the command-list window at +0x5A8 or resolves the widget's current command id and, when that command is set in the work bitmap at work+0x273FC, marks the render object dirty and unwinds the page stack.

evidence: The body is the shared popup + close sequence (Ui_BattlePopup_Show, func_002E037C on self[0x8d], Sound_PlaySeById, virtual +0x4C/+0x14) with no command-id switch, so it is a close-on-input handler rather than a 'command page' handler. The class prefix is fixed by the handler table and the self[0x8d]/self[0x4e] layout shared with the other slots.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCommandWindow_ResetPartyUnitStates
summary: Battle command window handler: when active and a selection is live it shows the battle popup, walks the battle party list at battleWork+0x4260 resetting each unit's display state through virtuals +0x5C/+0x60/+0x64, then requests sub-window state 9.
evidence: The party-list walk at battleWork+0x4260 and the three virtual resets are readable, and the preamble (self+0x405, inputMask & 0x102, self[0x8d], self[0x4e]) is identical to the other battle command window slots, so the Ui_PartyPanel_ prefix was wrong. What state 9 means is still unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCommandWindow_AdvanceScriptByCommand
summary: Battle command window handler: on a confirm event it shows the battle popup and switches on the pending command id at self+0x3FC, advancing the window script to the matching step (0x10/0x11/0x13/0x14/0x15/0x16) and hiding the target sub-window.
evidence: The clean switch on self+0x3FC with script steps 0x10..0x16 and the virtual +0x4C/+0x74/+0x68 calls are readable, and the handler sits directly before Ui_BattleCommandWindow_ExecuteSelectedCommand in the same table, which fixes the class; the per-step meanings are not established.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCommandWindow_ToggleProgressFlag
summary: Battle command window handler: on confirm it shows the battle popup and, when the sub-window has a live selection, inverts bit 0 of the GameWork progress byte at +0x2D384, then hides the panel and requests sub-window state 0xD.
evidence: The body inverts bit 0 of GameWork+0x2D384 and shares the exact preamble of the other battle command window slots, so the Ui_PartyPanel_ prefix was wrong; the flag is a general progress byte, so calling it an 'auto flag' was an unproven guess.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCommandWindow_ShowMessage8C2
summary: Battle command window handler: releases the auxiliary message layout, shows battle popup message 0x8C2, moves the window script to step 0x11, pumps the message window command list and re-links the window's own list node.
evidence: The body is short and fully readable: Ui_MessageWindow_ReleaseLayout(window[0x81]), Ui_BattlePopup_Show with 0x8C2, virtual +0x4C step 0x11, Ui_MessageWindow_ProcessCommands - so the action is certain even though the class prefix is inferred from the shared window layout (window[0x81], window[0x8d]).

name: Field_Gimmick_ScatterParts
summary: Scatters each part of a field gimmick around its actor group: it sets the group direction, then for every part adds a jittered offset from Field_Gimmick_GetRandomPartOffset plus the global RNG, clamps it to the group centre +/- 1.5, stores it at part+0x234 and plays SE 0xE4E/0xE4F.
evidence: The loop over func_00650D34(group, i) parts with Field_Gimmick_GetRandomPartOffset, the +/- 1.5 clamp around the group centre and the SE play by self+0x9C all match the name; the group record comes from func_004A1E00(gimmick->ownerActor), which is what makes it a scatter around the actor group.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_DistributePartEffects
summary: Spreads an effect configuration over a gimmick's parts, writing twelve effect parameters at +0x24C..+0x278 and switching the parts on; the readable C is heavily damaged, so the effect-distribution reading is an inference from the field offsets.
evidence: Nothing new: the body still has bad instruction data at 0x005DB5DE, 19 removed unreachable blocks and unaff registers, and its only named callee is Text_ApplyToSpanArray (itself a doubtful name). Kept as maybe_ with the same reading.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_UpdateSteering
summary: Field actor steering update: depending on the two field-mode flags at work+8 +0x44/+0x45 it either copies the actor's facing from func_00669D88, or integrates the turn rate, move-speed scale and forward speed by delta time and writes them back to the actor.
evidence: The body integrates turnRate / moveSpeedScale / forwardSpeed by delta time and writes them to the actor, and the flag pair at work+8 +0x44/+0x45 selects the branch; nothing in it names a chase target, so the old 'monster chase behaviour' reading is dropped. The body is damaged (literal-pool reads fRam003af260 etc.).

name: maybe_Battle2DUnit_UpdateMoveToTarget
summary: Per-frame 2D battle unit move step: it copies the actor position into self+0xE8..0xF0, then snaps to or blends toward the stored destination, cancels the balloon on arrival and pushes the result into the actor transform.
evidence: The move/blend logic and Battle_Ui_CancelBalloon on arrival are readable, but the class attribution (a 2D battle unit) rests on the surrounding block rather than on a vtable or a named caller, so it stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Camera_ApplyTransformToActor
summary: Applies a camera object's transform to the scene camera actor: it copies positionX/Y/Z into the actor at (work+8)->f_54 +0x1C, sets the actor's +0x118 update flag and derives the facing vector from the rotation quaternion (rotationX/Y/Z/W).
evidence: The body reads the camera actor from the field object manager (+0x54 -> +0x1C), copies the position and computes a direction from the quaternion; nothing in it touches the event system, so the 'Event_' prefix was unsupported. The recovered file has no dossier and no callers.

name: maybe_Battle2DUnit_UpdateSnapToTarget
summary: Final step of the 2D battle-unit movement: it writes the stored position (unit[0x37..0x39]) into the actor transform, restores the orientation, and when the facing dot against the stored direction falls below g_battleMoveFinishThreshold it commits the position, clears the pending flag and returns 1.
evidence: The body is fully readable and matches the name (position commit, std_Acosf facing test against g_battleMoveFinishThreshold, func_005E7848 anim reset, return 1 on commit); only the 'Battle2DUnit' class attribution rests on the surrounding block rather than a vtable or a named caller.

name: Actor_Action_Anim5Update
summary: Actor-action update that fetches animation-table entry 5 (func_0063D6B8(dm,5)) and applies it to the target actor through virtual +0x84, then computes the actor's position delta, rotates it into the actor frame and sets the node direction.
evidence: The body is short and fully readable: the animation-table index 5, the virtual +0x84 apply, the f_3e0-f_3c8 / +1000-f_3d0 delta and the func_005736A0 rotation into Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection. The name claims only what the code does (no Dragon-Jump attribution).

name: Field_ActorMotion_WalkToward
summary: Walk-toward action update: it snapshots the target actor's position (f_27C/f_280/f_284), applies animation parameter block 0x2B0DDC, picks one of six variants with the global RNG, then normalises the delta to the target and feeds the resulting step to the actor.
evidence: The body snapshots the target position, rolls func_0051B1FC(...,6) for the variant, calls func_005F7784(targetActor, variant, 1) and normalises the delta vector (fRam002b0de8 / sqrt) - i.e. it walks the actor toward the stored target. The recovered file has no dossier, but the body is readable.

name: Actor_Action_JumpBaseUpdate
summary: Common update of an actor jump action: it sets the jump height scale to 1/3 (or the global jump speed scale times 1/3 when the actor's +0x3F1 flag is set), derives the horizontal displacement from the actor's position delta, rotates it into the actor frame and stores it as the jump offset.
evidence: The body is fully readable: the 0x3EAAAAAB (1/3) scale, the maybe_g_actorDragonJumpSpeedScale override, the f_3e0-f_3c8 / +1000-f_3d0 delta and the func_005736A0 rotation into action->jumpOffsetX/Y/Z. The name claims only the jump-offset computation.

name: Battle_ActionUi_InitRowTransforms
summary: Initialises the transform state of the battle action-UI rows: for every row it zeroes the position (f_9C/f_A0/f_A4), sets the +0x118 update flag and pushes g_directionReferenceVector as the row direction.
evidence: The row loop over virtuals +0x48/+0x40 with the zero-vector write, the +0x118 flag and Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection(g_directionReferenceVector) is fully readable and matches the name; the two callers are still maybe_ Update2D/Update3D fragments, but the name does not depend on them.

name: Battle_ActionUi_ResetMemberActors
summary: Resets the displayed battle member actors: in mode 'M' it clears each row actor's model effect and plays animation 0x33, otherwise it restores each actor's saved transform (f_240..f_248 back into f_88..f_90) and commits the weapon model.
evidence: The two branches are readable and use named helpers (Model_CreateAttachedEffect, Gfx_Node_FaceObject, func_005E7848 with anim 0x33, func_0040AAF8 for the attached model); the mode byte is ui[0x497] == 'M'. The callers are still maybe_ Update2D/Update3D fragments.

name: maybe_BattleScene_LayoutPartyUnits_Tail
summary: Tail fragment of BattleScene_LayoutPartyUnits, split off by Ghidra at the non-returning std_ConstructArray call: it writes g_battleUnitSlotPos4 (with X and Y negated) into the unit node, sets the node's +0x118 flag from the flags word and pushes the resulting direction.
evidence: The assembly shows it continues 0x0060C530 in the same stack frame, so it is not an independent function; the decompilation is still damaged (unaff_r4/r5). The name already says it is a tail fragment.

name: maybe_Script_ArraySortSiftAlt
summary: Second copy of the Squirrel array-sort sift step: it compares two array slots either with Sq_VmObjCmp or through a comparator closure (Script_Vm_CallClosure with 3 args), swaps the 8-byte slots when the result is negative and continues the heap sift.
evidence: The comparator-closure path (Script_Vm_PushNull / Sq_VmPushNull / Script_Vm_CallClosure(f8c,3,1,0)) and the Sq_VmObjCmp path are both readable and match the name; the body is still damaged (unaff_r6) and there are no callers, so the 'Alt' distinction from its twin stays unverified.

name: Script_ReturnArg2
summary: Squirrel native epilogue that returns the second argument: it reads stack slot vm->f_34+1, validates it with Script_Vm_GetWeakRefVal, pushes it as the single return value and returns 1 (or -1 when the validation fails).
evidence: The 68-byte body is fully readable and reads exactly vm->f_34 + 1, so 'Arg2' is literal; it is the twin of Script_ReturnArg differing only in the validation helper. No caller is recorded (it is reached through the native binding table).

name: Script_Vm_FindBlockByOffset
signature: void* Script_Vm_FindBlockByOffset(void* vm, void* file, int extra, u32 blockIndex, u32 offset)
summary: Finds the block that contains a byte offset: it walks the vm's f_24 entries at f_28 (stride 0x14), range-checks the offset against entry+8/+0xC, skips blockIndex matches, positions the file at (entry[+0x10]+extra)*8 and returns entry[+4]+0x1C.
evidence: The body is fully readable and the single caller is Script_Vm_ResolveStackIndex, which treats the result as a stack-slot block; the 0x14-byte entry stride and the offset range check match the name exactly.

name: maybe_Script_ReturnNull
summary: Minimal Squirrel native epilogue: it pushes a single null value onto the VM stack and returns 1, i.e. the bound native returns null.
evidence: The 16-byte body is exactly Sq_VmPushNull() + return 1 (the vm argument is dropped by the decompiler); nothing reads the stack top, so 'ReturnTop' overstated it. The single caller is Actor2DWalkLocator, reached through the binding table.

name: maybe_Ui_CasinoPanel_RefreshRowAvailability
summary: Refreshes one row of the casino prize/shop panel: it lazily creates the panel's 0x2F sub-object, then compares the bag count with the row's quantity scale (x1/x10/x100, gold cap 0x0098967F) and pushes the matching row state through the bound control.
evidence: The 0x001E2xxx block is the casino poker/prize panel base class (Ui_PokerWindow_Ctor installs g_uiPokerWindowBaseVtable), so the 'PartyPanel' prefix was wrong; the body's gold-cap 0x0098967F, 1/10/100 scale, Ui_PanelMessage_UpdatePrices and Ui_Slot_BindControl calls are the price/quantity row refresh. No caller is recorded.

name: maybe_Battle_PartySlots_AssignActor
summary: Assigns an actor to a free battle party slot: it calls Menu_AssignActorToFreeSlot and, only in 3D battle mode (battleWork+0x4244), refreshes the slot through func_0020B990 and builds a 4x8-byte 0xFF-filled slot record array.
evidence: The body's first act is Menu_AssignActorToFreeSlot and the rest is the 3D-mode slot refresh plus std_ConstructArray(...,0x005906C0,8,4,0xFF); it notifies nothing, so the old 'NotifyChanged' name described no code. The five callers (party window refresh, target marker update, member visibility, member widget, effect colour) all place or refresh a slot.

name: Battle_RunTargetSelection
summary: Runs the default target selection for a menu slot: it walks the battle party list at battleWork+0x4260, picks the first unit in state 1 and the first unit whose virtual +0x80 returns 1, then fills a target record and invokes Battle_SelectTargetsThunk.
evidence: The party-list walk at +0x4260 with the two virtual predicates and the final Battle_SelectTargetsThunk call are readable, and the single caller is Menu_AssignActorToFreeSlot, which is exactly where a default target is needed.

name: maybe_Menu_ResolveActorTarget
signature: u32 maybe_Menu_ResolveActorTarget(MenuState* self, u32 actorId, u32 selectionValue)
summary: Builds the scratch target record used when an actor is placed in a panel slot: the readable C shows only the 4x8-byte 0xFF-filled std_ConstructArray, because Ghidra dropped everything after the mis-marked-noreturn 0x00100050 call.
evidence: Nothing new: the readable body is a single std_ConstructArray call (the known 0x00100050 noreturn artifact hides the rest), so the function's real work is invisible. The callers (Menu_AssignActorToFreeSlot, battle UI refresh, member widget) still support the 'resolve a default target' reading.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_DtorBase
summary: Second-stage teardown of a UI window: it stores the class vtable, re-links the inline intrusive lists, releases two layout refs, destroys the two 0x414-byte element chains and runs Ui_Object_DtorBase / Ui_List_Dtor / Pack_ReleaseHandle on the members.
evidence: The body is a generic UI window teardown (Ui_Object_DtorBase, Ui_LayoutRef_Release x2, std_destroy_range of 0x414-byte elements, Ui_List_Dtor, Pack_ReleaseHandle) and the vtable 0x00759388 is the shared UI base also used by Battle_Popup3D and Ui_SakusenWindow, so the SkillPanelWindow attribution was unsupported.
